title: Reflections and Rotations with Coordinates Checkpoint
description: Show that you can apply and explain coordinate rules for reflections and rotations.

questions.question: Point A(-7, 4) is reflected across the x-axis. What is A'?
questions.explanation: Across the x-axis, y changes sign while x stays the same: (-7, 4) -> (-7, -4).

questions.question: Point B(-5, -11) is reflected across the y-axis. What is B'?
questions.explanation: Across the y-axis, x changes sign while y stays the same: (-5, -11) -> (5, -11).

questions.question: Point C(-9, 2) is reflected across the line y = x. What is C'?
questions.explanation: Across y = x, coordinates switch places: (-9, 2) -> (2, -9).

questions.question: Point D(3, -10) is rotated 90° counterclockwise about the origin. What is D'?
Point E(12, -1) is rotated 270° counterclockwise about the origin. What is E'?
Triangle PQR has P(1, 3), Q(4, 3), and R(2, 6). It is rotated 180° about the origin. What is P'?
questions.explanation: A 180° rotation changes both signs, so P(1, 3) becomes P'(-1, -3).

questions.question: The rule (x, y) -> (-x, -y) can describe either a 180° rotation about the origin or a reflection across the origin.
questions.explanation: Both transformations produce the same coordinate image for a point, even though the geometric descriptions differ.

questions.question: Rotate F(-6, 8) 90° counterclockwise about the origin. Write F' as an ordered pair.
In one or two sentences, explain the difference between reflecting across the x-axis and reflecting across the y-axis.
questions.correctAnswer: Reflecting across the x-axis keeps x the same and changes the sign of y. Reflecting across the y-axis keeps y the same and changes the sign of x.
questions.explanation: The mirror axis stays fixed; the coordinate measuring distance away from that axis changes sign.

questions.question: A student rotates (2, 5) 90° counterclockwise and gets (5, 2). Explain the mistake and give the correct image.
questions.correctAnswer: The student only switched the coordinates, which is the reflection rule for y = x, not the 90° counterclockwise rotation rule. The correct rule is (x, y) -> (-y, x), so (2, 5) becomes (-5, 2).
questions.explanation: For 90° counterclockwise rotations, switching is not enough; the old y-coordinate becomes opposite in sign.
